question: A shopkeeper has ₹10 and ₹5 notes totaling ₹350. If he has 45 notes in total, how many ₹10 notes does he have?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let ₹10 notes = x ⇒ ₹5 notes = 45 − x

Total value = 10x + 5(45 − x) = 350

⇒ 10x + 225 − 5x = 350 ⇒ 5x = 125

⇒ x = 25

**∴ Answer = 25**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = 350, Total notes = 45

**Formula used:**

Form linear equations based on value and count

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let number of ₹10 notes = x

⇒ Number of ₹5 notes = 45 − x

⇒ Total value equation:

⇒ 10x + 5(45 − x) = 350

⇒ 10x + 225 − 5x = 350

⇒ 5x + 225 = 350

⇒ 5x = 125

⇒ x = 25

⇒ Number of ₹10 notes = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation Method

Use count and value equations together

Substitution Technique

Express one variable in terms of another

Shortcut Idea

Assume one variable and reduce equation quickly

Verification

Check both total number and total value conditions
